title: Decoding inner speech with a brain-computer interface
summary: In four people with severe motor and speech impairments, researchers found imagined-speech signals in the motor cortex and decoded them with machine learning. They also tested filters and a trigger phrase to limit unintended decoding. This is a proof of principle with implanted electrodes: free, rapid inner speech cannot be decoded accurately, and attempted speech remains more accurate.

evidence.tested: Imagined-speech signals were recorded from motor cortex in four participants with implanted electrodes and decoded in real time, with filters and a trigger phrase tested to limit unintended decoding.
evidence.unknown: The source states this is a proof of principle, free inner speech cannot yet be decoded accurately, and attempted speech remains more accurate.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning decoded the imagined-speech neural signals.
